feedback.problem:
Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $Π$ with equations

$$
l:r=⟨2,0,2⟩+t⟨3,2,-3⟩,\,Π:r\cdot ⟨5,-2,3⟩=6.
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
Let's write the equation of the line as

$$
r=⟨2+3t,2t,2-3t⟩.
$$

Now, substituting $r=⟨2+3t,2t,2-3t⟩$ into the equation of the plane, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot ⟨5,-2,3⟩ & =6 \\ ⟨2+3t,2t,2-3t⟩\cdot ⟨5,-2,3⟩ & =6 \\ 5(2+3t)-2(2t)+3(2-3t) & =6 \\ 10+15t-4t+6-9t & =6 \\ 2t & =-10 \\ t & =-5.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, position vector $p$ of the intersection point $P$ is obtained by substituting $t=-5$ into the equation of the line, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}p & =⟨2+3(-5),2(-5),2-3(-5)⟩ \\  & =⟨-13,-10,17⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the intersection point is $P(-13,-10,17).$
